s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, ulcerative, and bleeding skin lesion with purpuric patches and papules on the scalp and face
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Central ulceration and bleeding of the lesion
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: The lesion first developed in March 2014
Rapid growth and extension occurred in June 2014
The lesion is 30 × 25-cm in size
The lesion is centrally eroded and has purpuric plaque
No evidence of lymphadenopathy
Dermis is permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells have pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stain positively with CD31 and are negative for CK5
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors

shortlist.label: Cutaneous angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a rapidly growing, ulcerative, and bleeding skin lesion with purpuric patches and papules on the scalp and face, and histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31

shortlist.label: Kaposi sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the purpuric patches and papules, but less likely given the rapid growth and ulceration, and lack of evidence for human herpesvirus 8 infection

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to cutaneous angiosarcoma, but less specific to the skin, and the clinical presentation and histopathology are more consistent with cutaneous angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the rapid growth and ulceration, but typically has a more benign clinical course and lacks the characteristic histopathological findings of angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: A rare vascular tumor that could explain the clinical presentation, but is less common than cutaneous angiosarcoma and would require further diagnostic evaluation to confirm

raw.rationale: The large size of the lesion, rapid growth, and central erosion along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31 are consistent with cutaneous angiosarcoma

rejected.label: Kaposi sarcoma
rejected.why: While Kaposi sarcoma can present with similar skin lesions, the lack of lymphadenopathy and specific histopathological features make it less likely

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma is a more general term and cutaneous angiosarcoma is a specific subtype that matches the presentation and histopathology of the case

rejected.label: Pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Pyogenic granuloma typically presents as a small, solitary, rapidly growing lesion, which does not match the large size and extent of the lesion in this case

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma is a rare vascular tumor that can have a similar histological appearance, but the clinical presentation and immunohistochemical profile do not perfectly match this diagnosis
